mainTopic: Loans of produce and other cases of רבית: wheat loans, הלל's strict view, gifts between תלמידי חכמים, and trading farm work.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about lending wheat. רב ששת explains that it is talking about a loan where no price was set: if wheat gets cheaper the lender takes wheat back, and if it gets more expensive the borrower pays the old value. A new משנה forbids borrowing wheat to repay at harvest, because a price rise would be רבית. It allows a very short loan, like 'until I find the key', but הלל forbids even that, and even lending a loaf of bread without setting its value. The גמרא brings רב הונא and רבי יצחק on how owning some grain makes such a loan allowed, and רבי חייא's teaching supports רבי יצחק. שמואל rules like הלל, but the גמרא says the הלכה is not like him, and the חכמים let neighbors borrow and repay casually. שמואל then teaches about friends who are strict with each other when sharing meals, and says תלמידי חכמים may give each other extra on a loan as a gift. רב's idea of lending to one's family with רבית as a lesson is rejected. A new משנה closes the amud: neighbors may swap the same kind of farm work, but not different kinds.

steps.title: Lending wheat with a set price
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules on lending a כור of wheat with a price set. If wheat gets cheaper, the borrower returns wheat. If wheat gets more expensive, he pays the original money value.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone says, 'Lend me a כור of wheat,' and a price is set. If wheat gets cheaper, he gives back wheat. If wheat gets more expensive, he gives the money value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about a wheat loan where a money value was set at the start, and how to repay when prices change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is רבית. If wheat goes up and the borrower returns the same amount of wheat, the lender gets back more value than he lent. So when prices rise, he pays the original money value. When prices drop, the ברייתא says he may give wheat, and the next step will question that.

keyTerms.meaning: sets a price / fixes the money value

phrases.english: Lend me a kor of wheat
and he sets a price for him
if they became cheaper, he gives him wheat
if they became more expensive, he gives their value
phrases.notes: Their value means the money the wheat was worth back when he borrowed it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַלְוֵינִי כּוֹר חִטִּין וְקוֹצֵץ לוֹ דָּמִים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a wheat loan with a price set, cheaper wheat lets the borrower return wheat, and pricier wheat requires paying the original value.

steps.title: But a price was set
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: if a price was fixed, the borrower owes that money, so why can he return cheaper wheat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first half of the ברייתא. Once a price is fixed, the lender should get that full amount even if wheat gets cheaper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Setting a price turns the loan into a money debt. Returning wheat after the price dropped would short the lender. So the ruling 'הוזלו – he gives wheat' seems to contradict the price that was set.

keyTerms.meaning: but surely, isn't it so that (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But he set a price!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first ruling of the ברייתא in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that if wheat gets cheaper, the borrower may return wheat.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A fixed price makes the debt a money debt, so the borrower should owe the set value no matter what the market does.

steps.title: רב ששת: the case is where no price was set
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the ברייתא means a case with no price set. If wheat gets cheaper, the lender just takes his wheat back. If it gets more expensive, the borrower pays the original value.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: This is what it means. If he did not set a price: if wheat got cheaper, the lender takes his wheat. If wheat got more expensive, the borrower gives the value.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the challenge by rereading the ברייתא. It is talking about a loan where no price was set.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no price fixed, the deal was simply wheat for wheat, so if wheat drops the lender gets his wheat back. If wheat rises, returning the same wheat would give the lender extra, which is רבית, so the borrower pays the original value instead.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what it means (rereading the source)

steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת is not changing the law of a loan with a set price. He is saying the ברייתא's ruling belongs to a case where no price was set at all.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: This is what it is saying.
If he did not set a price
if they became cheaper, he takes his wheat.
phrases.notes: Here it's the lender who takes back his wheat.

phrases.english: if they became more expensive, he gives their value.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source (הכי קאמר): the ברייתא is about a case with no price set.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that even with a set price, the borrower may return cheaper wheat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling applies when no price was set. Cheaper wheat goes back as wheat, and pricier wheat is paid at the original value to avoid רבית.
steps.whatToRemember: With no price set: if wheat drops, the lender gets wheat back. If wheat rises, the borrower pays the original value so the lender does not gain רבית.

steps.title: No borrowing wheat to be repaid at harvest, but a short loan is fine
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids borrowing a כור of wheat to be repaid at harvest time. It allows borrowing until 'my son comes' or 'I find the key.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may not say to his friend: 'Lend me a כור of wheat and I will give it back to you at the threshing floor.' But he may say: 'Lend me until my son comes,' or 'until I find the key.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It forbids a long-term wheat-for-wheat loan, and allows a very short one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until harvest is a long time, and the price of wheat might rise. Then the lender would get back more value than he lent, which is רבית. A loan of a few moments, like until the son arrives or the key is found, leaves no real time for the price to change.

keyTerms.meaning: threshing floor; here it means harvest time

phrases.english: MISHNAH: A person may not say to his friend:
Lend me a kor of wheat
and I will give it to you at the threshing floor.
phrases.notes: When the new crop comes in at harvest.

phrases.english: But he may say to him: Lend me
until my son comes
or until I find the key.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יֹאמַר אָדָם לַחֲבֵירוֹ: הַלְוֵינִי כּוֹר חִטִּין וַאֲנִי אֶתֵּן לָךְ לַגּוֹרֶן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Borrowing wheat to repay at harvest is forbidden. Borrowing for a moment, until the son comes or the key is found, is allowed.

steps.title: הלל forbids even a short loan, and even a loaf of bread
steps.stepSummary: הלל forbids even the short loan. He also says a woman may not lend her friend a loaf of bread unless they set its money value, in case wheat goes up and they come to רבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And הלל forbids it. הלל would also say: A woman may not lend a loaf of bread to her friend unless she sets its money value, in case wheat goes up in price and they end up with רבית.
steps.whatsHappening: הלל disagrees with the first opinion in the משנה. He forbids even the short loan, and he gives a similar ruling about lending bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For הלל, any delay could bring a price rise, so even 'until I find the key' is not safe. The loaf case shows how strict he is: even a neighborly loan of bread needs a set money value. Then if prices rise, she pays back that value and not a pricier loaf.

keyTerms.meaning: until she sets its money value

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how far the rabbinic fear of רבית on produce loans can reach, even into ordinary favors between neighbors.

phrases.english: And Hillel forbids it.
phrases.notes: He forbids even the short loan, until the son comes or the key is found.

phrases.english: And so Hillel would say:
A woman may not lend a loaf to her friend
unless she sets its money value,
lest the wheat go up in price,
and they will be found coming to interest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion of the משנה about the short loan.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלל forbids even a short wheat loan, and requires setting a money value even when lending a loaf of bread.
steps.whatToRemember: First opinion: harvest-time wheat loans are forbidden and moment-long loans are allowed. הלל: even moment-long loans are forbidden, even a loaf of bread, unless a value is set.

steps.title: רב הונא: you may borrow as much as you already have
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that someone who has a סאה may borrow a סאה, and someone who has two סאה may borrow two.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: If he has a סאה, he may borrow a סאה. If he has two סאה, he may borrow two סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה. רב הונא gives a rule for when a wheat-for-wheat loan is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the borrower already owns that amount of grain, it is as if he could repay right now. The loan is treated like it was settled on the spot, so a later price rise does not count as רבית. רב הונא allows this only up to the amount he actually has.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmud's discussion of the משנה
a measure of grain, much smaller than a כור

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Huna said:
If he has a se'a, he may borrow a se'a.
If he has two se'a, he may borrow two se'a.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: יֵשׁ לוֹ סְאָה לֹוֶה סְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a condition for when a grain loan like the one in the משנה would be allowed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person may borrow grain to be returned in kind only up to the amount he already owns.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: one סאה is enough to borrow many כורים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק disagrees with רב הונא. Even if a person owns just one סאה, he may borrow many כורים based on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק says: Even if he has only a סאה, he may borrow several כורים on the strength of it.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion is given. רבי יצחק is far more lenient than רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יצחק, owning even a small amount is enough to allow the whole loan. He does not require the borrower's grain to match the full amount. This sets up a real disagreement with רב הונא about how much grain the borrower must have.

keyTerms.meaning: on it; relying on that one סאה
several כורים, a much larger amount

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak says:
Even if he has a se'a,
he may borrow several kor on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִצְחָק אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ לוֹ סְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב הונא in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Owning even one סאה is enough to borrow many כורים of grain to be returned in kind.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: you may borrow only as much grain as you have. רבי יצחק: having even a little grain lets you borrow a lot.

steps.title: A teaching from רבי חייא backs up רבי יצחק
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches that if a person has no drop of wine or oil, he may not borrow it. This implies that if he has even one drop, he may borrow many drops. That supports רבי יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught a ברייתא to support רבי יצחק: 'If he does not have a drop of wine, or does not have a drop of oil' (he may not borrow). This implies that if he does have a drop, he may borrow many drops based on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא from רבי חייא that backs up רבי יצחק's lenient view from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only forbids borrowing when the person owns nothing at all, not even a drop. So owning a single drop is enough to allow borrowing 'many drops'. That matches רבי יצחק, who said one סאה is enough to borrow many כורים. It goes against רב הונא, who allowed borrowing only as much as you own.

keyTerms.meaning: This implies; so it follows that

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya teaches
in support of Rabbi Yitzchak:
If he does not have a drop of wine,
phrases.notes: The words 'he may not borrow' are not written here, but they are understood.

phrases.english: or he does not have a drop of oil.
This implies: if he does have one,
he may borrow many drops based on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא לְסַיּוֹעֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רבי יצחק's position in his disagreement with רב הונא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יצחק's ruling that owning a small amount allows borrowing a large amount.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא taught by רבי חייא, read by inference: owning even one drop allows borrowing many drops.

steps.title: שמואל rules like הלל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'and הלל forbids' from the משנה. רב נחמן reports in the name of שמואל that the הלכה follows הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says 'And הלל forbids.' רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's words 'and הלל forbids' and gives שמואל's ruling that the הלכה follows הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הלל forbids even the short loan, like 'until my son comes'. שמואל says the הלכה is like this strict view. The very next line will reject this ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: The final ruling follows the words of

phrases.english: And Hillel prohibits.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה about the short loan, 'until my son comes'.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Shmuel said:
The halakha follows the words of Hillel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלֵּל אוֹסֵר. אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רב הונא and רבי יצחק discussion and returns to the משנה's next clause, about הלל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to שמואל, the הלכה follows הלל, who forbids even short loans of produce.

steps.title: The final ruling does not follow שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the הלכה is not like שמואל's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the הלכה is not like him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final word: we do not follow שמואל's ruling that the הלכה is like הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since שמואל's ruling is rejected, the practical הלכה follows the lenient view of the משנה. You may borrow produce for a short time, like 'until my son comes'.
steps.whatToRemember: In practice, we do not follow הלל's strict view. Short loans of produce, such as 'until my son comes', are allowed.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Like him' refers to שמואל's ruling, which is the ruling the גמרא is turning down.

phrases.english: But the halakha is not like him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is שמואל, so we do not follow his ruling to be strict like הלל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the ruling given in step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה does not follow הלל here. Short-term loans of produce are permitted.

steps.title: The חכמים disagree with הלל about the loaf of bread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes הלל's rule from the משנה that a woman may not lend a loaf unless its value is set. שמואל says this is only הלל's view. The חכמים allow borrowing and repaying without setting a value.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And so הלל used to say: a woman may not lend a loaf to her friend, etc.' רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: this is הלל's view. But the חכמים say people may borrow without setting a value and repay without setting a value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes הלל's loaf-of-bread rule from the משנה. Then שמואל says that the חכמים disagree with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הלל worried that the price of wheat might go up, and then repaying a loaf would be רבית. The חכמים allow casual borrowing and repaying between neighbors without fixing a price. So the strict loaf rule belongs to הלל alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Without saying anything specific; without setting a value

phrases.english: And so Hillel would say:
A woman may not lend, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' points to the rest of the משנה: a loaf to her friend, unless they set its value.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
This is the view of Hillel,
but the Sages say:
One may borrow without specifying, and repay without specifying.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הָיָה הִלֵּל אוֹמֵר: לֹא תַּלְוֶה אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the משנה's next clause about הלל and shows that the חכמים disagree with him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים allow borrowing and repaying items like bread without setting a value. Only הלל forbids it.

steps.title: Friends who share meals and are strict with each other
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says that a group of friends who eat together and are strict about exactly who owes what run into several problems. They break the rules against measuring, weighing and counting, and against lending and repaying on יום טוב. According to הלל, they also run into רבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: members of a group who are strict with each other violate the rules of measuring, weighing and counting, and of lending and repaying on יום טוב. And according to הלל, they also violate the rule of רבית.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a new ruling about a group of friends who share meals and keep exact track of what each one owes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because these friends care about exact amounts, sharing food becomes real measuring and real lending. This causes problems on שבת and יום טוב. According to הלל, repaying food in kind can also become רבית. This only applies when they are strict; casual sharing is fine, like the חכמים in the step before.

keyTerms.meaning: Members of a group (who eat together)
Who are strict and care about exact amounts

steps.whatToRemember: The problem comes from being strict with each other. When friends are not strict, borrowing and repaying casually is allowed, as the חכמים said.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּנֵי חֲבוּרָה הַמַּקְפִּידִין זֶה עַל זֶה,
phrases.english: Members of a group who are strict with one another,
transgress because of measuring,
phrases.notes: Measuring, weighing and counting are problems when done on שבת or יום טוב.

phrases.english: and because of weighing, and because of counting,
and because of lending and repaying on a Festival,
and according to Hillel, also because of interest.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: בְּנֵי חֲבוּרָה הַמַּקְפִּידִין זֶה עַל זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling from the same chain, רב יהודה in the name of שמואל, applying הלל's view to friends who are strict with each other.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Friends who share meals and are strict about exact amounts violate the rules of measuring, weighing, counting and lending on יום טוב. According to הלל, they also violate רבית.

steps.title: Torah scholars may borrow from each other with interest
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reports in the name of שמואל that תלמידי חכמים may borrow from one another with רבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: תלמידי חכמים are allowed to borrow from each other with רבית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of שמואל about רבית. This one gives a surprising leniency for תלמידי חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally any extra payment on a loan is forbidden רבית. Here שמואל says that between תלמידי חכמים it is allowed. The reason comes in the next step.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a general permission to charge interest. It applies only to a special case, and the reason in the next step explains why.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Torah scholars are permitted
to borrow from one another with interest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching of שמואל on רבית, following his teaching about the group of friends in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תלמידי חכמים may borrow from one another with רבית.

steps.title: The reason: the extra is a gift
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that תלמידי חכמים know רבית is forbidden, so the extra they pay is meant as a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? They surely know that רבית is forbidden, so the extra is a gift they give each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why שמואל allowed this and answers right away. Because scholars know the law, the extra money counts as a present, not as payment for the loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What makes רבית forbidden is that the extra is paid for the loan. Since תלמידי חכמים know that is not allowed, we assume they never meant it as payment for the loan. The extra changes from forbidden 'interest' into a permitted 'gift'.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
They surely know that interest is forbidden,
and it is a gift that they give one another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind שמואל's ruling in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why are תלמידי חכמים allowed to borrow with רבית?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They know רבית is forbidden, so the extra is meant as a gift.

steps.title: שמואל borrows peppers from אבוה בר איהי
steps.stepSummary: שמואל asks אבוה בר איהי to lend him 100 peppers and promises to return 120, saying this is proper.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to אבוה בר איהי: Lend me 100 peppers for 120 peppers, and it is fitting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing that שמואל acted on his own ruling. Between two scholars, he openly offered to give back extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Returning 120 for 100 would normally be plain רבית. שמואל calls it fitting because, as step 14 explained, between תלמידי חכמים the extra twenty is a gift.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לַאֲבוּהּ בַּר אִיהִי:
phrases.english: Shmuel said to Avuh bar Ihi:
Lend me one hundred peppers
for one hundred and twenty peppers, and it is fitting.
phrases.notes: שמואל is telling him not to worry: this is proper, since the extra twenty are a gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לַאֲבוּהּ בַּר אִיהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows שמואל himself practicing the ruling of step 13.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that תלמידי חכמים may borrow with רבית
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's own conduct with אבוה בר איהי
steps.whatToRemember: Between תלמידי חכמים, extra paid on a loan is treated as a gift, not as forbidden רבית, because both know רבית is forbidden.

steps.title: Lending to one's family with interest to teach a lesson
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reports in the name of רב that a person may lend to his children and household with רבית so they learn how bitter it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A person may lend to his children and household with רבית, so that they will taste what רבית is like.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second leniency, this time from רב. A father may charge his family רבית as a lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is educational. If the family feels how painful it is to pay back extra, they will stay away from borrowing with רבית later. The next step rejects this ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: the taste of interest, how hard it is

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
It is permitted for a person
to lend to his children and the members of his household with interest,
in order to let them taste the taste of interest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case where רבית might be allowed, after the case of תלמידי חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person may lend to his family with רבית to teach them how hard it is.

steps.title: Rejected: the family may get used to it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב's ruling, because the family members may become drawn into dealing with רבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is not correct, because they may come to get used to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב's teaching from step 16 and says it is not the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lesson could backfire. Instead of learning to avoid רבית, the family might get used to it and deal with it with others too. So the danger outweighs the lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: to get drawn in / become used to it

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a lesson cannot be taught in a way that risks training people in the very sin it is meant to prevent.

phrases.english: But this is not correct,
because they will come to get used to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the ruling of רב in step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole ruling that one may lend to his family with רבית
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The family may get used to רבית instead of learning to avoid it.
steps.whatToRemember: The ruling of רב about family loans is rejected; we worry the family will get used to רבית.

steps.title: משנה: trading the same farm work, not different work
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that two people may swap the same kind of field work, like weeding for weeding, but not different kinds, like weeding for hoeing.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may say to his friend: Weed with me and I will weed with you, or hoe with me and I will hoe with you. But he may not say: Weed with me and I will hoe with you, or hoe with me and I will weed with you.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It applies רבית to trading work instead of money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying back a work day with the same kind of work is fine. Paying it back with a different kind of work is forbidden; the usual explanation is that one job may be harder, so one person ends up giving back more than he got, which is like רבית.
steps.confusionAlert: Both kinds of trades are paying back work with work. The only difference is whether the two jobs are the same kind.

phrases.english: MISHNAH
A person may say to his friend:
Weed with me and I will weed with you,
hoe with me and I will hoe with you.
But he may not say to him:
Weed with me and I will hoe with you,
hoe with me and I will weed with you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹמֵר אָדָם לַחֲבֵירוֹ: נַכֵּשׁ עִמִּי וַאֲנַכֵּשׁ עִמָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, moving from loans of money and goods to exchanges of work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Exchanging the same type of field work is allowed; exchanging different types is forbidden.
